interviewQuestions.question: How does HashMap work internally in Java 8?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: Array of Node buckets. Hash calculation: (key.hashCode() ^ (h >>> 16)) & (n-1). In Java 8, when bucket length exceeds TREEIFY_THRESHOLD (8) and capacity >= 64, linked list converts to Red-Black tree (TreeNode), reducing worst-case lookup from O(N) to O(log N).

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between ConcurrentHashMap and SynchronizedMap?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: SynchronizedMap locks the entire collection on every read/write. ConcurrentHashMap (Java 8) uses CAS (Compare-And-Swap) for empty bucket insertion and synchronized on the bucket head node for collisions, allowing concurrent reads and segmented concurrent writes without full table locking.

interviewQuestions.question: Bean lifecycle in Spring Framework?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: 1. Instantiation -> 2. Populate Properties -> 3. BeanNameAware / BeanFactoryAware -> 4. BeanPostProcessor (postProcessBeforeInitialization) -> 5. @PostConstruct / InitializingBean (afterPropertiesSet) -> 6. Custom init-method -> 7. BeanPostProcessor (postProcessAfterInitialization) -> 8. Ready for use -> 9. @PreDestroy / DisposableBean -> 10. Custom destroy-method.

interviewQuestions.question: How to handle distributed transactions across Microservices?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: Use Saga Pattern (Orchestration vs Choreography). Two-Phase Commit (2PC) is synchronous and causes blocking/latency. Saga uses compensating transactions to rollback intermediate state if a subsequent step fails.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is String immutable in Java?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: 1. Security: used in network connections, database URLs, class loading. 2. Thread-safety: shared across threads without synchronization. 3. String Constant Pool optimization: caching saves memory. 4. Hashcode caching: hashCode calculated once and cached for fast Map operations.

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between WHERE and HAVING clause?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: WHERE filters rows before aggregation (cannot use aggregate functions). HAVING filters group rows after GROUP BY aggregation.

interviewQuestions.question: Process vs Thread and how Context Switching works?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: A Process is an executing program instance with its own virtual address space, memory, and file descriptors. A Thread is a lightweight execution unit inside a process sharing the same address space but with its own stack and program counter. Process switching incurs TLB cache invalidation overhead; thread switching within the same process does not.

interviewQuestions.question: What is @Transactional and how does Spring manage rollbacks?
interviewQuestions.answerSnippet: Uses Spring AOP dynamic proxy to intercept method calls and begin/commit transaction with PlatformTransactionManager. By default, rolls back only on unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and Error), NOT on checked exceptions unless rollbackFor = Exception.class is explicitly configured.

projects.title: Enterprise Microservices E-Commerce Platform
projects.starSituation: Existing legacy monolith suffered frequent checkout timeouts during festive sales and had single point of failure bottlenecks.
projects.starTask: Architect a distributed high-throughput microservices backend supporting 5,000 requests/sec with 99.9% uptime and zero order data loss.
projects.starAction: Decomposed monolith into Order, Payment, Inventory, and Notification services using Spring Boot 3. Implemented Saga pattern with Kafka for distributed transactions, Redis for distributed locking (Redisson), and resilience patterns via Resilience4j circuit breakers.
projects.starResult: Reduced P99 latency from 450ms to 42ms. Achieved 99.95% uptime during peak load tests with zero double-booking errors.
projects.architecture: Client -> Spring Cloud API Gateway -> Eureka Discovery -> Microservices (Order, Payment, Inventory) -> Kafka Event Bus + Redis Cache + PostgreSQL
projects.challenges: Preventing double-booking of inventory under 5,000 requests/second concurrent load.
projects.performance: Reduced average P99 API response time from 450ms to 42ms using Redis caching & async Kafka processing.
projects.testing: 85%+ JUnit 5 test coverage, Mockito for unit testing, Testcontainers for integration tests.
projects.deployment: Deployed on AWS EKS using Helm charts and GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline.

crossQuestions.question: How did you handle distributed transactions across Microservices without 2-phase commit?
crossQuestions.myAnswer: Used the Saga Pattern with orchestration. Each microservice publishes events to Kafka, and if a downstream service fails, compensating transactions are published to roll back state.

crossQuestions.question: How did you prevent Redis cache stampede/thundering herd during flash sales?
crossQuestions.myAnswer: Used Redis distributed lock (Redisson) for cache miss calculation combined with jittered TTL expiration times.
